config.title: Mini Redux

intro.title: Mini Redux
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simplified version of Redux, a state management pattern, using Vue's built-in reactivity system. You'll learn how to create a centralized store to manage your application's state in a predictable way. The core concept involves implementing actions and reducers to update state, ensuring changes are made through a single, controlled flow. You'll use Vue's reactive() and computed() functions to handle state and getters, along with basic JavaScript objects and functions. By the end, you'll have a working mini Redux store that can be integrated into a Vue component, helping you understand the fundamentals of state management in larger applications.
intro.usecase: The state management pattern taught in this lesson is the foundation for complex, interactive applications like e-commerce dashboards. In these dashboards, user actions such as filtering products, updating cart quantities, or toggling admin panels must reliably update the UI and sync data across components. Implementing a mini-Redux system helps manage these predictable state transitions, preventing bugs in scenarios like multi-step checkout forms or real-time data visualizations. Mastering this pattern equips you to build scalable features where many UI elements depend on a single source of truth.

objectives: Construct a Vue component that initializes and manages a centralized state object
Implement a dispatch function that processes actions to update the application state
Configure reactive state updates that trigger automatic UI re-rendering
Bind UI elements to state properties using Vue's reactive system
Integrate action creators that generate standardized payloads for state modifications
Manipulate state immutably by returning new state objects from reducer functions
Control state access through a predictable unidirectional data flow pattern

steps.title: Import Vue and reactive from Vue
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the reactive function from the Vue package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and reactive from 'vue'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing from a package
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue framework and reactive function are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: Vue and reactive are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Vue and reactive from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import both Vue and reactive from the 'vue' package.

steps.title: Create a createStore function
steps.instruction: Define a function named createStore that accepts two parameters: reducer and initialState.
steps.hint: Start with 'function createStore(reducer, initialState) { }' or use an arrow function.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue and reactive from 'vue'

// Define createStore function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A createStore function is defined with the correct parameters.
successCriteria: The createStore function is defined and accepts reducer and initialState as parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function is named createStore and accepts both reducer and initialState parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The createStore function isn't defined correctly. It should accept reducer and initialState as parameters.

steps.title: Initialize reactive state in createStore
steps.instruction: Inside the createStore function, use Vue's reactive function to create a reactive state object from the initial state parameter.
steps.hint: Call reactive with the initial state to make it reactive and store the result in a variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating reactive state
const state = reactive({ count: 0 });
steps.expectedOutcome: The createStore function will have a reactive state variable initialized from the initialState parameter.
successCriteria: A reactive state variable is created inside createStore using the initialState parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the reactive function with the initialState parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reactive state wasn't properly initialized. Remember to use Vue's reactive function with the initialState parameter inside createStore.

steps.title: Add getState method to store
steps.instruction: Inside the createStore function, add a getState method that returns the current reactive state object.
steps.hint: The getState method should be a function that returns the state variable you created in the previous step.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createStore function now has a getState method that returns the reactive state, allowing external code to read the current state.
successCriteria: The createStore function contains a getState method that returns the state variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a getState method inside createStore that returns the state variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The getState method is missing or incorrect. Add a getState method that returns the state variable inside createStore.

steps.title: Add dispatch method to store
steps.instruction: Inside the createStore function, add a dispatch method that takes an action parameter and calls a reducer function with the current state and that action.
steps.hint: The dispatch method should be a function that accepts an action object and passes it to a reducer along with the current state.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createStore function will have a dispatch method that can be used to update state through actions.
successCriteria: The createStore function includes a dispatch method that accepts an action parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added a dispatch method inside createStore that takes an action parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The dispatch method is missing or incorrectly placed. Add a dispatch method inside the createStore function.

steps.title: Update state in dispatch method
steps.instruction: Inside the dispatch method, update the reactive state object by assigning the reducer's return value to it. The reducer receives the current state and the action as arguments.
steps.hint: Use the reducer function to compute the new state based on the current state and the action, then assign that result back to the state object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The dispatch method will now properly update the reactive state when called with an action.
successCriteria: The dispatch method contains code that calls the reducer with current state and action, then assigns the result to the state object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling the reducer with both the current state and the action, then assigning the result to the state object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The dispatch method should update the state by calling the reducer with the current state and action, then assigning the return value to the state object.

steps.title: Create a counter reducer function
steps.instruction: Create a function named counterReducer that takes state and action as parameters and returns the updated state based on the action type.
steps.hint: The reducer should check action.type and return a new state object with count updated accordingly. For 'INCREMENT', increase count by 1; for 'DECREMENT', decrease count by 1; otherwise return the current state unchanged.
steps.expectedOutcome: A counterReducer function is defined that handles 'INCREMENT' and 'DECREMENT' actions to update the count state.
successCriteria: counterReducer function exists, takes state and action parameters, and returns updated state based on action.type.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a reducer function, but check that it properly handles both 'INCREMENT' and 'DECREMENT' actions and returns the updated state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The counterReducer function is missing or doesn't follow the reducer pattern. Make sure it takes state and action parameters and returns updated state based on action.type.

steps.title: Create main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named App with a template and script section. The template should contain a root <div> element.
steps.hint: In Vue, a component can be defined as a function that returns an object with template and script properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a basic Vue component structure ready to build upon.
successCriteria: An App component function is defined with a template containing a root <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main Vue component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the App component has a template with a root <div> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component is not properly defined. Check that it has a template with a root <div>.

steps.title: Initialize store in component
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's setup function, create a store instance by calling createStore with an initial state object that has a count property set to 0.
steps.hint: Use createStore with an object like { count: 0 } as the argument.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing a store
const store = createStore({ value: 10 });
steps.expectedOutcome: The store instance is created with an initial state containing count: 0.
successCriteria: The store is initialized inside the App component's setup with the correct initial state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling createStore with an object like { count: 0 } inside the App component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store initialization is missing or incorrect. Please create a store instance with an initial state containing count: 0.

steps.title: Display current count in template
steps.instruction: In your App component's template, add a paragraph element that displays the current count value from your store's state. Access it using store.getState().count.
steps.hint:
Inside the return statement, add a

tag with the count value. You can use template syntax to display it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show the current count value (initially 0) in a paragraph.
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists in the template that displays store.getState().count.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a paragraph, but make sure it displays the count value from store.getState().count.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph displaying the count is missing or incorrect. Check that you're accessing store.getState().count in the template.

steps.title: Add increment button and wire dispatch
steps.instruction: In the App component's template, add a button element with the text 'Increment' and wire its click event to dispatch an INCREMENT action using the store.
steps.hint: Add a <button> element inside the template object. Use @click to call store.dispatch with an object containing type: 'INCREMENT'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a button that, when clicked, dispatches an INCREMENT action to the store.
successCriteria: A button element with text 'Increment' is added to the template, and its @click event calls store.dispatch with { type: 'INCREMENT' }.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a button with the text 'Increment' and that its @click handler calls store.dispatch with the correct action object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button or click handler isn't quite right. Check that you've added a button element with @click="store.dispatch({ type: 'INCREMENT' })" inside the template object.

steps.title: Add decrement button and wire dispatch
steps.instruction: In the App component's template, add a second button with the text 'Decrement' that dispatches a DECREMENT action when clicked.
steps.hint: Add a <button> element next to the existing increment button. Use @click to call store.dispatch with an object containing type: 'DECREMENT'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button @click="store.dispatch({ type: 'DECREMENT' })">Decrement</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have two buttons: one that increments the count and one that decrements it, both wired to dispatch their respective actions.
successCriteria: A 'Decrement' button is added to the template with an @click handler that dispatches a DECREMENT action.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it dispatches the correct action type 'DECREMENT' when clicked.
steps.feedbackWrong: The decrement button is missing or not properly wired to dispatch a DECREMENT action.
